task.title: Maintaining Secure Cloud Storage and Services
task.shortdesc: Promoting security and privacy of cloud storage and services to prevent unauthorized access and theft of personal data.

taskbody.context: Cloud services, such as Microsoft OneDrive, iCloud, and Google Drive, enable real-time collaboration and allow you to back up your data. While cloud services offer convenience and can facilitate data backup, they also carry the risk of increased opportunities for cyber attacks, less control over your data, and potential for your data to be lost. To prevent these risks, adhere to the following best practices:

step.cmd: Use end-to-end encryption to protect your data as it moves between your device and the cloud service.
Use strong encryption to protect your data when it is stored on cloud servers.
Use a strong password and MFA to make it more difficult for threat actors to access your cloud account.
Ensure your cloud provider is headquartered in a country with privacy and security laws that help protect your data.
Keep updated copies of critical data on devices you physically control, such as your computer or an external hard drive, to reduce the risk of permanent data loss.
Be vigilant against phishing attempts to trick you into clicking on a link and entering your cloud account credentials.
Keep your device and software updated to reduce the chances that a threat actor can access your cloud account through malware installed on your device.
Manage account permissions so that only those who need access to documents in the drive have it.
Ensure that anyone with access to the cloud service protects their account with a strong password and MFA and is trained to recognize phishing attempts.

info.note: You can typically find this information on the cloud service provider’s website.
